title: Reply: God foresees obedience or defiance only as following his earnest warnings, which are means to obedience
source_text: XX. Sed tantum abest ut praevisa hominum contumacia, vel obedientia obstet quominus Deus serio illos monere, rogare, & hortari possit: ut contra Deus illam non possit praevidere, quin prius praevideat, & apud se constituat se ita serio cum hominibus acturum. Nam divinae monitiones, hortationes, & obtestationes sunt media quibus procuratur hominum obedientia; & praesupposita quaedam, sine quibus Deo rebelles, & in ipsum contumaces esse & dici non possunt.
pass_a_gloss: But so far is it from being the case that the foreseen stubbornness, or obedience of men hinders God from being able seriously to admonish, ask, and exhort them: that on the contrary God cannot foresee it, without first foreseeing, and determining with himself that he will deal thus seriously with men. For divine admonitions, exhortations, and adjurations are means by which the obedience of men is procured; and certain presuppositions, without which they cannot be and be called rebels to God, and stubborn against him.
pass_b_english: Far from preventing God from earnestly warning, asking and exhorting human beings, their foreseen defiance or obedience is something God cannot foresee without first foreseeing, and resolving within himself, that he will deal with them earnestly in this way.

God's warnings, exhortations and pleas are the means by which human obedience is brought about. They are also presupposed conditions without which people cannot be, or be called, rebels against God and defiant toward him.

lemmas.gloss: first foresee, and determine with himself

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
